claims.quote: ChatterMate is an open-source AI customer-support chatbot platform
claims.statement: The platform is open-source: its source is available under an open-source licence.

locations.quote: ChatterMate is an open-source AI customer-support chatbot platform

statements: ChatterMate is an AI customer-support chatbot platform: the core function of that category — an AI chatbot for customer support — exists.

claims.quote: You can sign up, create AI agents, add knowledge sources, and embed a chat widget
claims.statement: The platform supports the listed capabilities: sign-up, creating AI agents, adding knowledge sources, and embedding a chat widget.

claims.quote: all from a browser, the terminal (CLI), or programmatically via an AI agent over MCP
claims.statement: The whole workflow can be done through each of three channels: a browser, a terminal CLI, and programmatically by an AI agent over MCP.

locations.quote: embed the chat widget on any site

claims.quote: the `chattermate` command, installed with `pip install chattermate-cli`
claims.statement: A CLI named `chattermate` exists and is installed by the PyPI package `chattermate-cli`.

locations.quote: let an AI agent configure ChatterMate over the Model Context Protocol (`chattermate-mcp`)

claims.quote: to sign up and manage everything from the terminal
claims.statement: The CLI supports signing up and managing the account and configuration from the terminal.
The `chattermate` CLI's role is account and configuration management.

claims.quote: distinct from the self-host Docker tool (`npm install -g chattermate-deploy`)
claims.statement: A separate self-host Docker tool exists, distributed as the npm package `chattermate-deploy`, and is distinct from the `chattermate` CLI.

claims.quote:
chattermate signup --name "Acme Inc" --domain acme.com --admin-email you@acme.com --admin-name "You"
chattermate agent create --name "Support" --type customer_support -i "Be concise" --json
# Add knowledge from a URL or a local PDF:
chattermate knowledge add-url --website https://docs.acme.com --agent-id <agent-id>
chattermate knowledge add-file ./guide.pdf --agent-id <agent-id>
# Create a widget to get the embed id:
chattermate widget create --agent-id <agent-id> --name "Website widget"
claims.statement: The `chattermate` CLI supports the subcommands shown in the flow — `signup`, `agent create`, `knowledge add-url`, `knowledge add-file`, `widget create` — with the options shown, and they carry out the stated effects (signup, agent creation, adding knowledge from a URL or local PDF, widget creation returning an embed id).
The chat widget is embedded on a site by setting `window.chattermateId` and loading the script served at https://app.chattermate.chat/webclient/chattermate.min.js.

claims.quote: the account CLI — signup, login, tokens, agents, workflows, knowledge
claims.statement: The CLI's command areas include signup, login, tokens, agents, workflows and knowledge.
Widgets support authentication, and programmatic tokens can be issued (the Widget Apps feature).
A hosted API is served at https://api.chattermate.chat with its routes under `/api/v1`.

claims.quote: run the full stack on your own infrastructure with the self-host CLI
claims.statement: The self-host CLI runs the full ChatterMate stack on the user's own infrastructure.
The `chattermate-deploy` CLI has the subcommands `init`, `start` and `stop`.
